text.p: Australian bonds underperformed other dollar bloc bonds after today's A$800 million Treasury bond tender failed to inspire the market to rally from its pre-tender lows.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread grew to its widest level in almost a week and over 10 basis points above the low seen immediately after last week's benign wages data.
The U.S. market faces the release of the third quarter employment cost index later today, the first of several key economic indicators this week.

Meanwhile, an initial tightening to Canada was also reversed going into the close. The Canadian market remained in corrective mode on Monday with a further 25 basis point easing by the Bank of Canada having been widely expected.
A recovery in the New Zealand dollar after last week's sharp sell-off helped to support N.Z. debt, particularly the short-end, and outperform the local market.
